strategies.name: mean_reversion_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: On an in-play stock that has stretched too far too fast into a clearly defined support or resistance level, wait for order-flow hesitation at the level (e.g. volume stalls, sellers stop hitting the bid, or large bids/offers hold). Then take the opposite side of the move: get long in front of support
strategies.exit_summary: Use the bids/offers at the support or resistance level as protection and exit by capturing the bounce/reversal off that level; the stop/protection is tied to losing that level/order-book support.

variants.variant_label: long bounce off sharp flush into support
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: volume stalls and sellers stop hitting the bid at support; large bids help confirm
variants.transcript_quote: On a sharp down move into support, you will often see a moment where volume stalls, and it's this pause where people stop hitting the bid. As a scalap

variants.variant_label: short fade off sharp squeeze into resistance
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: sharp move into resistance with large offers
variants.transcript_quote: Often, these mean reversion scalps work best when the stock quickly and sharply shoots up to a resistance level with large offers.

strategies.name: continuation_breakout_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: On an in-play stock consolidating beneath clean resistance or above clean support, enter on the actual break once tape confirms aggressive participation and the level gives way. For example, buy just above resistance like $10.01/$10.02 or $50.01 after the offer is taken.
strategies.exit_summary: Scalp out into the immediate emotional follow-through after the breakout or breakdown. Use a tight stop back through the broken level, e.g. stop if price gets back below the breakout resistance.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: be first in on the break of clean support/resistance
variants.transcript_quote: if we have a $10 resistance level, you want to be buying $10.01 or $10.02, and scalping out on that emotional follow-through

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: buyers repeatedly lift $50 offer, offer shrinks and disappears
variants.target_note: kick it out 10, 20, or even 30 cents higher
variants.transcript_quote: If buyers continue lifting and the offer size begins to shrink, then suddenly it's gone, you want to be the one buying at $50.01

variants.target_note: stop right below the broken level if it falls back under
variants.transcript_quote: Often, your stop loss would be right below that level if it gets back below the $50.

strategies.name: spread_making_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: In a liquid but spread-out name, provide liquidity rather than taking it by placing resting limit bids/offers ahead of large bids or offers to capture the bid-ask spread as urgent traders cross. The edge comes from market microstructure, not directional prediction.
strategies.exit_summary: Sell/lift out at the other side of the spread once filled, capturing the spread or a point or two, and repeat while the spread remains wide before it compresses.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: resting limit orders, queue priority, hidden vs visible order awareness
variants.target_note: capture the difference between bid and offer as participants cross
variants.transcript_quote: You're placing resting limit orders in spread names ahead of large bids or offers with the aim to capture the difference between the spread

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: slam in huge bids during wide, active spread
variants.target_note: kick offers out a point or two higher and repeat before spread compresses
